text:
Maya: quick sync — we need to lock the perf launch criteria for the "resource-slicing" runtime work (kernel fallback + kv prefetch + quant combos). Sales flagged a customer ask: 99th <150ms on 2048 context and embeddings throughput >=2 r/s per GPU. Can the team surface whether that's realistic without dedicated pooling?

Priya: short answer: maybe. Early 4-bit quant runs lower cost but we see tail spikes when fallback to slower kernels happens. KV prefetch helps for steady-state but hurts short bursts. Need controlled benching across 3 configs.

Omar: can you share the early numbers? also need to know what "tail" means here (p50/p95/p99).

Priya: pasted quick run from my laptop (toy, not lab):
```
config A: fp16 no-prefetch -> p50 34ms / p95 98ms / p99 230ms (2048)
config B: 4-bit + prefetch -> p50 40ms / p95 110ms / p99 160ms
config C: 4-bit + kernel-fallback enabled -> p50 38ms / p95 105ms / p99 175ms
```
Takeaway: quant helps average cost, prefetch reduces p99 in stable workloads but can increase queuing when bursts hit. Kernel fallback keeps correctness but increases p99 in some traces.

Alex: noted. I'm concerned about the interaction with batching policies — our continuous batching window currently increases latency variance. For a launch we should specify batching knob defaults and an escape hatch.

Santiago: SRE perspective — launch criteria must include a canary burn (72h) and an SLI deck: p99 latency, tail error rate, and CPU/GPU mem pressure. Error budget <=1% during canary. Also add an automated rollback if p99 regresses >20% vs baseline.

Maya: draft launch criteria proposal: 1) perf baseline established on representative customer traces; 2) canary 72h with regression <5% p99 vs baseline; 3) KV prefetch and quant profile documented and tested; 4) kernel fallback exercised in canary with correctness tests; 5) rollout staged by traffic slices + manual approval. Does that feel reasonable?

Omar: yes but + add a cost-impact check (tokens/sec per GPU and cost delta). Sales will want a number.

Priya: also ask product: require Customer QA prompt set run as part of canary for their critical prompts — catches quality regressions from quant.

Maya: added. Owner suggestions: Omar -> bench runs and canary infra; Priya -> quant + quality validation; Alex -> rollout knobs / batching defaults; Santiago -> SLO automation / rollback. Deadline: benches + initial canary config by next Wed (2024-07-10).

Omar: I'll run microbench with 3 configs (fp16 baseline, 4-bit+prefetch, 4-bit+fallback) across 2048 and 4096 contexts. Will post artifacts + perf scripts.

perf-bot: canary job started: perf-canary/2240536789 on cluster 'canary-us-east' — monitoring p50/p95/p99 and gpu_util.

Alex: I pushed a small telemetry change that tags requests by rollout-slice; that'll help isolating noise during the canary.

Santiago: reminder: ensure we have alerting on slow-allocs and mem-evictions — those correlate with p99 spikes.

Maya: great. If we get the bench numbers by Wed we'll convene a 30m decision huddle Thurs morning to finalize whether this goes into Q2 launch window. Thanks all :thumbsup:
